**PROPOSED ENGINEERING SOLUTION: Active Thermal Compensation System**

**Design/Indicator:** Real-time spindle temperature monitoring with closed-loop thermal compensation
- Temperature sensors at 3 critical bearing locations (front, middle, rear)
- Thermal expansion coefficient-based displacement model
- Real-time compensation of tool center point (TCP) position via CNC axis adjustment

**Thresholds:**
- USER CONSTRAINT: TCP displacement must remain <10 μm during 20-minute warmup (given)
- CALCULATED: Maximum allowable temperature gradient between bearings = 2.5°C (based on steel thermal expansion coefficient ~12 μm/m/°C and 10 μm displacement limit over 400mm typical spindle length)
- ASSUMPTION: Spindle thermal time constant = 8 minutes (typical for precision spindle bearings)

**FALSIFICATION TEST:**

**Protocol:**
1. Cold start spindle at 20°C ambient temperature
2. Record baseline TCP position using laser interferometer
3. Run spindle at maximum rated speed (e.g., 15,000 RPM) with no load
4. Record temperature at all 3 sensor locations every 10 seconds
5. Measure TCP position every 30 seconds using laser interferometer
6. Repeat for 3 consecutive warmup cycles

**Measured Quantities:**
- Temperature at each bearing location (°C)
- TCP displacement in X, Y, Z axes (μm)
- Time from startup (seconds)

**Explicit Thresholds:**
- PASS: TCP displacement remains <10 μm in all axes for entire 20-minute warmup
- FAIL: TCP displacement exceeds 10 μm in any axis at any time during warmup
- KILL CRITERION: If displacement exceeds 15 μm at any point, test fails and design requires revision

**Standard Practice Comparison:**
Standard practice typically uses fixed warmup cycles (15-30 minutes) with no active compensation, resulting in equivalent or worse performance. The proposed solution adds:
- 3 temperature sensors (~$500)
- Thermal model software integration (1-2 weeks development)
- No additional hardware required for compensation (uses existing CNC axes)
- Implementation cost is ~10% of alternative solutions (spindle redesign or cooling system)

**Feasibility Grounding:**
1. Unit consistency: 
   - Thermal expansion: 12 μm/m/°C × 0.4m × 2.5°C = 12 μm (within 10 μm constraint)
   - Temperature measurement resolution: 0.1°C sufficient for 2.5°C gradient threshold
2. Test executability:
   - Laser interferometer can measure to 0.1 μm resolution
   - Temperature logging at 10-second intervals captures thermal transient
   - Clear pass/fail criteria with quantitative thresholds
3. Hardware requirements:
   - Temperature sensors: Standard PT100 elements with appropriate mounting
   - No additional mechanical hardware required
   - Software integration with existing CNC system

The proposed solution meets the constraint without adding warmup idle cycles and is feasible with standard industrial components and integration practices.
